problem.scope: Authored in-process concurrency study: a fixed-capacity circular buffer with one lock versus a linked FIFO with separate put/take locks and an atomic count. Both use condition variables, predicate loops and explicit wakeup rules. Java's Condition redirects a signal when it lets an interrupt win over that signal; on condition variables without that rule, an interrupted waiter that may have absorbed a signal re-tests its predicate and signals again before propagating. Graph modules are local synchronization/state responsibilities, not network services. No persistence, process recovery or unconditional fairness claim.

evidence.testName: batch-08 queue: blocked predicates wakeups close and cancellation

acceptanceCases.given: Capacity one, producer P1 fills, P2 waits, consumer removes; plus enumerated put/take orders for capacities one to three.
acceptanceCases.then: The predicate loop keeps P2 blocked while full; after the removal it publishes exactly one item; every enumerated order keeps FIFO data and size within capacity.
acceptanceCases.when: Wake P2 spuriously before the removal, then notify after removal, and drain each enumerated queue after close.

evidence.testName: batch-08 queue: blocked predicates wakeups close and cancellation

acceptanceCases.given: A waiting producer, an empty queue with a waiting taker, and a close.
acceptanceCases.then: The canceled operation mutates nothing; closure resolves every waiter; put after close is rejected; takes drain the remaining item before closed-empty.
acceptanceCases.when: Cancel the waiting producer, close, then attempt put and take.

evidence.testName: batch-08 queue: interrupted waiter passes a consumed signal on

acceptanceCases.given: Two takers waiting on notEmpty on a condition variable that does not redirect signals; one put signals the first taker.
acceptanceCases.then: The interrupted taker finds an item and signals again; the second taker wakes and takes the item; interrupting an unsignaled waiter signals nobody.
acceptanceCases.when: Interrupt the signaled taker before it returns to the lock.

guarantees: No busy waiting; all predicate rechecks occur under the owning mutex; an interrupted waiter never strands another waiter whose predicate holds.

evidence.testName: batch-08 queue two-lock: lock order and crossing signals

acceptanceCases.given: Capacity two filled until full, then alternating takes and puts, plus 400 seeded put/take operations on capacity three.
acceptanceCases.then: put on a full queue and take on an empty one change nothing, as each would wait on its own lock's condition; items leave in FIFO order and count stays within capacity; the empty-to-nonempty put signals notEmpty holding only takeLock, and the full-to-nonfull take signals notFull holding only putLock.
acceptanceCases.when: Run them through the two-lock transitions while recording each lock acquisition and signal.

evidence.testName: batch-08 queue two-lock: lock order and crossing signals

acceptanceCases.given: The same recorded trace, including close.
acceptanceCases.then: The only nested acquisition is close taking takeLock while holding putLock; no put or take path ever holds both locks.
acceptanceCases.when: List every acquisition made while another lock was held.

evidence.testName: batch-08 queue two-lock: lock order and crossing signals

acceptanceCases.given: A closed two-lock queue that still holds one item.
acceptanceCases.then: put reports closed; the first take drains the remaining item and the second reports closed-empty; no lock remains held.

acceptanceCases.given: A producer links a node and increments the atomic count while a consumer polls under takeLock.
acceptanceCases.then: It reads the linked node's item, never a null next. This relies on the platform's release/acquire guarantee and is not exercised by the single-threaded reference model.
acceptanceCases.when: The consumer observes count > 0 with acquire semantics.

evidence.testName: batch-08 queue: interrupted waiter passes a consumed signal on

acceptanceCases.given: Two consumers waiting on notEmpty on a condition variable that does not redirect signals; a put signals one of them.
acceptanceCases.then: It re-tests count, signals notEmpty again, and the other consumer takes the item.
acceptanceCases.when: The signaled consumer is interrupted before it returns to takeLock.

guarantees: Count provides cross-lock publication; crossing signals occur after releasing the local lock; only close nests locks, in putLock-then-takeLock order.
